thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: auth-service.jwt.validate.errors > 5% in eu-west-1 for 120s. Pager: PD#auth-prod.

oncall-eng: acked pagerduty — taking lead, will triage now.

mike.lee: seeing a big spike in 401s on the hosted API. Dashboards show error-rate jump at 02:12 UTC. Can anyone confirm impact scope?

sara.khan: confirmed. Alerts from the EU edge show ~2.3% of token validations failing for oauth and API-key flows. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. 

carol_ops: rolling logs: many failures are `jwt: invalid signature` and `kid not found` on validation. JWKS requests show 503s from jwks-cache in eu-west-1 for a short window.

oncall-eng: paging PD logs — first page at 02:12:03, second at 02:12:40. PID trace attached in the dashboard (link: https://redwood.ops/trace/abc123). Looks like a JWKS mismatch: validators hitting an old keyset while signer rotated.

mike.lee: reproduction: curl to token-introspect gives `kid` header with key id `k_2026_042`. Validator rejects because its local JWKS cache doesn't contain that kid.

sara.khan: quick check: KMS replication had a lag during the rotation window; signer pushed new public key to control-plane, but cache invalidation TTL is 5m and our invalidation event didn't propagate to eu-west.

oncall-eng: mitigation plan: 1) revert signer to previous key (fallback) 2) force JWKS cache refresh across regions 3) throttle rotate window and disable auto-rotate temporarily. Who can flip fallback?

mike.lee: I can flip fallback to previous key now. Doing `authctl rollback-key --id k_2026_042 --to k_2025_998` (running).

incident-bot: deploy-bot: starting rollback job auth-signer/rollback/2026-03-14T02:15Z. Job: 7 pods will be restarted.

sara.khan: issuing cache refresh: `curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/v1/refresh-jwks?scope=eu-west-1` to all config controllers, rolling now.

carol_ops: confirmed: JWKS cache refreshed for eu-west-1 at 02:16:10. Validators now see `k_2025_998` in set. 401s dropping.

oncall-eng: monitoring... error rate back to normal baseline ~0.1% at 02:17:40. Customer-facing impact: approx 11 minutes of elevated 401s in eu-west-1, affecting ~1.8% of requests in that region. No data exfiltration.

mike.lee: paging PD: closing incident with note: temporary key rollback completed, JWKS cache refresh applied, auto-rotate disabled pending postmortem.

carol_ops: leaving notes for SRE runbook updates: add explicit cache-invalidation webhook to signer rotation flow, add TTL reduction for JWKS cache during rotations, add a pre-rotate propagation check step.

oncall-eng: handing off to night-shift (sara) for monitoring & postmortem follow-up. @sara.khan — take it.

sara.khan: taking it — will run impact query and start a short postmortem doc at https://docs.redwood/incidents/2919990000. Will include RCA and timeline.

mike.lee: quick customer comms draft for CS: "We observed a brief validation error causing transient 401s after an automated key rotation. We rolled back the key and refreshed caches; the service is healthy. We're updating the rotation process to prevent recurrence." PTAL @carol_ops.

carol_ops: LGTM. Add exact timeframe and affected endpoints before sending. Also tag enterprise accounts that hit eu-west-heavy routes.

incident-bot: Note: incident severity assessed S2 (partial degraded service). Incident closed by oncall-eng at 02:18:00.

oncall-eng: closing thread — will aggregate logs and open a follow-up for the full postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
